newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish govt/unions agree to raise jobless benefit.
newsitem.headline: Swedish govt/unions agree to raise jobless benefit.

text.p: Sweden's minority Social Democrats government and umbrella union organisation LO on Wednesday agreed to increase unemployment benefits to 80 percent from 75 percent of a worker's former wage from October 1, 1997.

"The agreement is entirely financed within the framework the the current rules from the unemployment benefit fund," Labour Minister Margareta Winberg said in a joint statement published in conjunction with LO.
"The main part will be financed through an increase in fees for members of the fund which will be raised by 22 crowns per member per month," she said.
The government and LO also have agreed to a proposed three-year time limit on unemployment benefits.
